title: Biased probability respects event equivalence
statement: Let $\rho\in\bbr$, let $m$ be a natural number, and let $A,B$ be predicates on finite Boolean words. If $A$ and $B$ agree on every word of length $m$, then their probabilities under $m$ independent bits that are true with probability $\rho$ are equal.
hypotheses_covered: $A$ and $B$ are predicates on Boolean words
$A(w)$ is equivalent to $B(w)$ for every word $w$ of length $m
